summary: I'll check how this project formats session summaries so the paragraph matches that style.The party remains split across two clocks, with the faster lighthouse group setting the pace: about six of their days have passed while Walker has lived roughly forty-two on the Reach, still inside the Midgar-week window before his leftover time is montaged. At the ruined Dragon Rider keep, Walker waits until a notice says a deity has left, then returns with Glimmen to an empty roost. Clockwise-shifted cave etchings name a grassy atoll, Mount Elcastar, and Monkey Falls; Elrus explains the Weave and ley lines and reads the offset as a moved convergence Grixto found, a deadly pairing with the Al Kurin and the Raskina for lichdom. After meditation, the hunched eagle troop marker flashes the stone table into a partial battle map whose obelisk sits fifteen degrees off true, which they take as a conveyance worth checking, and Elrus offers primal stones at the risk of Walker losing part of himself. Meanwhile Ord, Gerk, and Sylan leave Carlkin’s lighthouse after a bitter fight: Carlkin, a former gatekeeper, warns them to deal at once with the telepathic lich, explains that Gerk’s keyless doors must always be closed, and tells him to practice only in open country. Gerk breaks down when he hears that as an order to discard his mother’s keepsake. After a night in New Navel they train in the southern forest. Doors land near a known place or a person Gerk has just seen, fail when Ciri’s exact spot is unknown and open onto a trench of explosions, and a rage-opened door grows enormous and shears branches clean when two portals form a vortex. A small door into a tomato field lets something growl and ram the shut panel until Gerk lets go. They ride back to Langdale Stronghold around midday, having learned he can open portals seemingly at will, with sharp limits.

plotSections.title: Split clocks
bullets: The party is split. Walker is on the Reach; Ord, Gerk, and Sylan are at Carlkin's lighthouse on the same day. The group moving faster in time is the controlling clock.
Walker told them he would be back within about a week of their time. When that week runs out, his leftover Reach time is montaged and he rejoins them, unless he ends the side scene early.

During the lighthouse scene the DM's working count is about five days and a morning of party time since the split, with Walker having lived about eleven days. The rate is settled the next morning: seven of Walker's days equal one party day. By then about forty-two of his days have passed, six party days, so the Midgar-week check-in is not yet due and the party is not worried.

plotSections.title: Walker at the Dragon Rider ruins
bullets: Walker's thread resumes from the earth, wind, sea, and fire sigil. He has spoken with Vecna, which the DM frames as opened communication, possibly a book club.

He is in the ruins of the Dragon Rider guild keep, comparing the view with notes from drawings in the cave below. All he has is a rotated image of an obelisk, an island, a waterfall, and a mountain peak, and he believes there is more downstairs. From the old tower those landmarks are shifted radially off their true positions.

He left the cave because Vecna was there and will not go back until Vecna is gone. He will not write in the book to ask whether Vecna is still below. How he would know is unresolved until a ping arrives.

He waits a couple of hours. Plymouth Gawater is still on site, scribing and taking etchings. Walker asks Glimmen whether Vecna is still down there. A notice says a deity has left the realm, and Walker and Glimmen go back down.

plotSections.title: The empty roost
bullets: The smell has faded to a faint linger. The room is empty: no one at the table, the chair pushed back, and the troop marker Vecna had been tapping still on the table. The rest of the room is as Walker left it.

The landmark drawings are cave etchings carved around the room in order, a panorama that does not follow the cardinal directions. Every sketch is rotated the same way clockwise. Walker thinks the shared offset is a clue, and the DM confirms he is onto something. The etchings correspond to a location above. There is no map, no compass, and no manifesto.

The table is a flat stone slab about four feet by four feet, not a map carved into the surface. Three more stone chairs are carved like the table. The room is an empty roost with those furnishings, the etchings, and troop markers scattered on the floor.

The markers are black stone and ivory, though the material might be a dark metal or bronze. They include knight-like cavalry pieces, small etched dragons, pawn-like pieces marked for rank or unit size, and flat poker-chip tokens in two matched sets. The piece Vecna left on the table is a high-ranking hunched eagle on a decorative base, not one of the chips. Walker sets the other pieces on the table and keeps the eagle.
A troop marker taken off a table in the earlier vision is not here. That vision is how the party connected the scene to the Raskina.

plotSections.title: Landmarks, the Weave, and the moved convergence
bullets: Walker assumes Elrus has been shadowing him the whole time, and that is confirmed. Elrus names the etched landmarks: an unnamed flat island of rolling green plains, about the size of the island they are on and sometimes written as the grassy atoll; Mount Elcastar; and Monkey Falls, marked by an old obsidian ley-line marker. The landmark Viablis has stood since Elrus was a boy and is only rumored to be a ley line, so Elrus finds it concerning that Grixto carved it into the wall.

Walker has not been taught the Weave or ley lines. Elrus says the Weave is the magical network around them, briefly visible as a flash when energy is used, and ley lines are concentrations of it formed over ages. Some credit Atlas's rotation; others treat them as a magical latitude and longitude. They are not a tunnel network between planes. Standing on a line bolsters spells, teleportation and other magic cost less energy, and casting at an intersection is like stepping into a fire pit while already on fire: low-level spells perform higher.

Markers can drift over millennia. Mages sought the lines out and fought over them, so many markers were moved or hidden. A spell has to be cast within feet of a convergence. Convergences are rare; Elrus has seen only a few.

The clockwise shift is the point. The carving shows where the old obsidian marker or intersection would be, and the rotated position is where the convergence is now. Grixto found this ley line, and the line had to have been moved. Elrus means to visit soon if the rest of their business comes to nothing, because knowing this convergence would matter. Walker calls it the clearest lead they have had. Elrus says they have only been in the cave a few hours and blames the time dilation for how long it feels.

plotSections.title: Lichdom
bullets: Walker asks whether a lich is made by a spell or by simply designating an object, using a glove as the example. Elrus does not know the exact ritual. Phylacteries are usually gems of some kind, and the working is ancient.

Elrus ties Grixto's Al Kurin to lichdom. Ley-line knowledge would help a lich by strengthening magic, not by carrying anyone between planes. He says the Al Kurin, a ley-line convergence, and the Raskina together are a deadly combination.

plotSections.title: The eagle and the meditation
bullets: Elrus dismisses the troop markers as unnecessary. The fancy eagle fits a legion standard, and Grixto was a hobgoblin, whose legions would carry an eagle. Without a map he cannot say what the figurines are for. Walker still feels he is missing something. He pockets the eagle.

Elrus sits cross-legged in the middle of the cave and has Walker set aside what he is holding and meditate on the rituals Grixto laid out: where Walker must go, what he needs to get there, and the puzzle in front of him. He coaches nose-and-diaphragm breathing, a wave-like breath, and a sense of the floor. Walker follows. Elrus offers to sit for several hours. The scene leaves them meditating.

plotSections.title: Carlkin on gatekeepers, keystones, and the lich
bullets: Play resumes with Ord, Gerk, and Sylan at Carlkin's lighthouse, a second NPC also present. Sylan made no agenda and expects to spitball. They have already told Carlkin that the party holds keystones, that Gerk is a doorman who opened a door in the room onto the abyss, and that they are hunting a lich whose phylactery is a mundane item he kept on his person. They have already nearly brought an abyssal leviathan into the shop.

Sylan hoped Carlkin's knowledge and long time in the area would mean he knew something. Carlkin speaks for people who were once gatekeepers. They were given keystones and told to hide them. Their old job was protection, and they were not doormen. He finds it strange that keystones are being handed out again after so much effort spent collecting them. A lich speaking to the party telepathically alarms him, and he tells them to deal with that immediately.

Gerk's doors come from nothing and do not need a keystone. He can pass through his own door and open or close it from either side, and only he can close it. An unclosed door stays a gateway until the space-time continuum collapses. He is both Doorman and gatekeeper; Carlkin jokes that he could be called a gate doorman or a portcullis man. Only the Doorman can open that kind of portal.

Keystone gates work only in certain situations and are one-way. The keystone becomes part of the gate it opens, so it cannot be carried through. Other travel exists: plane shift, dimension door, teleport, teleportation circles, and Navi methods, including a small rod that teleports directionally across Atlas.

Carlkin tells Gerk to practice somewhere empty, such as the woods or a large field, never underwater and not in the lighthouse. He will mend the damaged floor himself and thanks them for trying to fix it. He is drinking. Sylan wants to practice at the castle, away from onlookers. Carlkin prefers the mountains, where no one can interfere. Gerk mentions dragons there, and Sylan mentions a previous giant fight. Carlkin has heard a rumor that the dragon is dead.

plotSections.title: Leaving the lighthouse
bullets: Gerk keeps trying to level the hole he made, tapping the floor by hand after Carlkin told him to stop. He is upset because he asked for help in his own way, Carlkin did not listen, and the damage is now treated as Gerk's fault. Carlkin compares him to a toddler in a sandbox and says the floor is nearly level.

Sylan apologizes for the floor, the door, and the trouble they have caused. Carlkin would rather they make an appointment than drop in. Gerk had been opening doors to get the party in before he understood he should not, and he refuses to take further risks with them.

Carlkin tells him that if the danger is that severe he should stay away from actual doors, and that he should immediately put down the thing that is dropping his arm. Carlkin meant Gerk's doorway ability and his durability, not the ordinary lighthouse door. Gerk still tries to climb out a window.

Gerk takes the demand to put the thing down as being told to discard the last memory of his mother. Carlkin, drunk and still reeling from an eldritch horror in his living room, says Gerk's mother will not come through the portal, but everyone else will. Gerk breaks down, tears streaming, visibly about to rage, and has to be dragged out babbling. He says Carlkin called out him and his dead mother at least three times and that he might punch Carlkin one day.

Sylan thinks Gerk may need healing and considers taking him back down through the floor with just the door. He walks Gerk out through the ordinary door and closes the doors behind them. He asks that when their comrade returns, Carlkin's people look at a helm. Carlkin agrees and will set the appointment by runner. They are much farther than five hundred feet from the castle, so it is a walk rather than a sending. The party is outside at midday.

plotSections.title: Day six in New Navel
bullets: Outside Carlkin's lighthouse at midday, New Navel is busy. It is the party's sixth day, with a day and a half left before a deadline the DM does not finish naming.

Sylan wants to rest, wait to hear from Walker, and then train Gerk's doorway on short distances. Gerk worries something will go wrong. Sylan says they solved it last time; Gerk notes that was with violence. Gerk suggests opening onto Carlkin's living room. Sylan puts that off until tomorrow because Carlkin told them not to use doors in his house. Gerk's distinction is that he would not be inside the house when he opened one.
Ord, Sylan, and Gerk go to the party's pub rather than straight back to the stronghold. Ciri is already in the corner, too drunk to keep stealthing, crouched as if hidden behind a pile of mugs.

The night is a drinking montage. The basement is finished and can hold cold storage. Owners are not charged. Locals recognize the party, and newer faces include travelers and traders from Dullhurst and beyond, in town for trade at New Navel and Rita. A middle-aged half-elf minstrel plays a classical lute while moving through the room instead of staying on a stage. The tavern manager is recalled as Flavian. They wake the next morning in the stronghold to the building shaking and the smell of fresh buns.

plotSections.title: Morning at Langdale Stronghold
bullets: Morning at Langdale Stronghold: the sun is up, the stronghold is shaking, and fresh buns are baking. Sylan, Gerk, Ord, and Ciri are in the great hall. Sylan has already been up for four hours. Ciri is face-down in the buns.

The check-in Walker agreed to is one Midgar week of the party's time, not a week of his own. At seven of his days to one of theirs, about forty-two of his days have passed and he is not overdue. He is expected to arrive by dragon. Mahali is asked to have food ready for Glimmen.

After breakfast Sylan starts Gerk's doorway training. Gerk questions why Sylan is the one to train him, looks to Ord mid-bite of a bun, then accepts and asks whether Ord is coming. Ord comes to watch.

plotSections.title: Into the southern forest
bullets: Ciri spent the night in a room at the tavern. She meets the others on the path back to the stronghold, still in the same clothes with her boots over one shoulder, and leaves with them.

They will not practice in the living room, because Gerk might open a portal to hell there. The lake has no island. They are not going to the bees, and they rule out old buildings and other civilization. Sylan suggests the southern forest clearing and stream from the earlier hobgoblin search. The DM ties previously found runes, heard as Paulette runes, to a red-flag marker a decent way into the forest. The party does not go to the runes. They only mean to enter the forest out of view of the stronghold. Gerk has no preference between dirt and stone.

Sylan tells the guards that the group went south into the forest and that Walker may contact them. Walker is expected on Glimmen, and the guards are asked to have Mahali prepare food for the dragon. By mid-morning the group is on the outskirts and ready to practice.

plotSections.title: Targeting a place
bullets: Before the attempt they restate Gerk's rules: picture something very specific, do not think of nothing, never open underwater, always close the door, and do not open it while moving.

Gerk focuses on a spot about twenty feet out from the tavern door, in the field in front of the tavern, still within Langdale, and says the target aloud. Sylan calls on the Raven Queen and grants Guidance. Gerk rolls a 16.

The door opens about a quarter mile southwest of the intended spot, near the road from the tavern to New Navel. From it they can see the tavern in the distance and, at that angle, most of the stronghold.

Sylan hops through and waits before having the door closed. Three human traders with a mule-drawn cart, about a football field away and headed the other way, are startled when he appears out of nothing. The portal faces away from them. They, and nearby guards, keep walking and only glance back. Sight and sound pass through: Sylan can see Gerk, Ord, and Ciri and can hear them. From the destination side the opening is a stationary, featureless, door-shaped hole, like a green screen projecting the people on the other side. Sylan calls the attempt close enough and treats portal magic here as unsurprising.

plotSections.title: Targeting Sylan
bullets: Sylan proposes targeting a person instead of a place. Gerk closes the door and focuses on Sylan, whom he knows is in this realm and whose general location he knows. He aims about ten feet behind him, close but not too close, and describes it as wanting to be near his best friend at a respectful distance. He also did not want to head back without Sylan.
Gerk rolls a natural 20. The door opens exactly as specified, about ten feet behind Sylan. There is no flash and no visible frame. The only sign is sound from the forest they left, including birds.

Sylan concludes the doorway can work on a person as well as a place. Gerk says knowing Sylan's general location helped. Sylan suggests fondness may also play a part; Gerk allows that it might. Later they tie the success more to Gerk having just seen him than to fondness alone. Sylan dusts off, waits out the traders, and hops back through.

plotSections.title: The hidden Ciri and the battlefield
bullets: Sylan asks whether it still works if Gerk does not know where the person is, and has Ciri hide in the woods. Her stealth check is a 7 on the die and a 23 total. Gerk covers his eyes. He still knows she is somewhere in the forest, not her exact spot, and aims for about a ten-foot circle around her. Sylan casts Guidance again.

The doorway roll is a 1 on the guidance die and a 3 on the d20, total 4. The door still opens, onto a maelstrom of explosions, flashes, and noise, opposite the quiet forest. In a trench embankment, an orc with a metal weapon crouches beside a human. Both wear mixed medieval and French Renaissance clothing and carry metal tube-sticks. One points a tube and shouts in a language the party does not know; the other fumbles a small clay pot from his belt.

Gerk slams the door. The forest returns: birds, cool air, a brimstone-sulfur whiff, and a black smudge on the grass. No other trace of the battlefield remains. He did not find Ciri. Sylan's working theory is that a person alone is not enough; the location has to be known, at least so far.
Sylan tells Ciri the attempt failed and she can come back or not. She throws her voice to answer, then stays hidden in a tree and watches.

plotSections.title: Remembering a door
bullets: Sylan frames the next step as training what activates the ability: emotion, rage, a happy memory, or a precise recollection of a place, including how it smelled. Gerk calls making him angry a bad idea. He says he is weak at describing places but will try. Sylan does not want to open a door home yet because the mission is unfinished. He names Halo Heart as a good place to picture, but not to open here.

They try Volga as a memory exercise: the frozen gatehouse they climbed, tall and cold, a little spooky, and the spear-in-the-head moment. Gerk only half remembers it. He chooses a tavern he has visited often and associates with friends instead. He calls it Twin Peaks; the group also says Bouncing Betty, and they cannot agree on the name, whether it has two floors or three, or whether a stage they remember belongs to a different place. Sylan says the rooms have been moved.

They aim for the upstairs hallway outside the rooms, the picture of leaving an inn bedroom into that hall, rather than the front door, which would drop them into a busy street. Sylan casts Guidance. Gerk rolls a 19, 16 plus 3. The DM had expected a miss and was not sure the tavern had a second floor. In game it has been a long time. They stopped once before the voyage toward Lake Nyx, a boat trip of about one to two months. Sylan remembers that stop as picking up Plymouth for the Yowan and hiding the last keystone until they arrived; it is also tied to a dragon.

The doorway does open on Bouncing Betty, but confusion shifts it onto a stronger memory. Gerk comes out on the second story of the rebuilt barn, about twenty feet from the upstairs hallway, looking down on stables and a wagon in the center. He has slept in that barn. He also remembers a sideline there: a wayward bard and a drunk wizard levitated and killed a mule or donkey, left the body, and the party made some gold. He shuts the door before anyone can fall. It clicks and disappears. Sylan calls it a strong result for somewhere so far away, and a sign that places Gerk likes are easier to hit.

plotSections.title: Opening a door by force
bullets: Sylan thinks Gerk may simply improve with use, or that something in him still has to be unlocked. He recalls Carlkin saying the party would not be able to open doors, and Plymouth Gawater saying that with time and practice they could use the keystones. Sylan does not intend to practice that yet. He says he has plenty of time and mentions his realm. Gerk refuses to let a key anywhere near him and says he will not fall for that trick again. The DM asks, "Again?"

Sylan suggests Gerk tap the same strength he uses to swing his hammer. Gerk agrees to open the door as hard as he can. Sylan sets a lantern about twenty feet away as a focus and steps back. Gerk turns his back, pictures that lantern, rages, and rips the doorway open. Guidance is on the attempt. He rolls a 17.

An enormous narrow door tears open, about eighteen feet tall and seven feet wide, much larger than his usual doors. It does not open onto the lantern. The far end is in the same forest roughly a quarter mile south, marked by a disturbance of birds. Where the doorway cuts through canopy branches, those branches sit in a semi-translucent limbo. Gerk can feel the door he opened and, separately, the presence of its far end.

Sylan treats the size as possible evidence that opening harder makes a bigger door, and notes that a door this size might fit Glimmen. Gerk is unsure but hopes that is how it works. Sylan does not trust the portal enough to step through first. He and Ciri walk the quarter mile south. The far side reaches into the canopy, intersecting branches are translucent, and the forest floor is undisturbed: no crater and nothing catastrophic. Sylan still does not know what caused the racket. They return through the portal, Ciri passing as a shadow, and come out beside Gerk. Sylan suggests Gerk may need to know a place fondly, or remember it fondly, to place the exit accurately. Gerk does not know whether he can open a door beside himself or what his exact range is.

plotSections.title: Two doors and a cutting close
bullets: They try an easier placement next: a normal, non-rage opening at a spot Gerk can see, about twenty-five feet away across a crossing and past the lantern. Sylan calls for Guidance. Gerk rolls a 9. The door opens short of the chosen spot, over the lantern, and is again about eighteen feet tall. The first door is still open.

Wind rushes between the two doors. The lantern is pulled through the new door and into the far eighteen-foot door as a vortex forms. Gerk shuts both doors and the wind dies. To the south, branches and limbs crash to the ground.

Where branches had passed through the doorway, they are cleanly severed, with no burn marks and no leftover debris, as if sliced by a blade. The fallen limbs lie in a pile. Sylan's lantern is dinged and disheveled from being sucked through, but not shattered.

They treat the shear as extremely dangerous. A closing door could cut a creature, a rope bridge, or anyone at a destination, and it might be useful against something huge. They agree not to use it in a crowded place or when opening onto a person. Gerk recalls Carlkin telling them to practice in the middle of a field. They were lucky the earlier kitchen opening did not cut Mahali, which the DM calls a critical success, and they connect the effect to the boat that was ripped out of reality. The doorway, opened three times a day, seems to surface recent destinations as favorites. Recent places may be easier. Gerk does not want another try yet; Sylan says they have time.

plotSections.title: The tomato field
bullets: Sylan wants a doorway toward his sister so they can get in and out quickly. Gerk refuses, citing the attempt to reach Ciri without knowing where she was. Sylan suggests Dana's boost and songs, or another spell, if they can learn which ability the door uses. Gerk says it just happens. They already know a forceful opening makes a bigger door.

Gerk instead tries a gentle, low, dog-sized door about a hundred feet in front of a house with tomato fields, clear of the plants. Sylan gives Guidance. Gerk rolls an 18. The opening is about six to eight inches by twelve inches, but it lands in the tomato field rather than the open ground, about a foot off the ground, where it can cut a stem. It is fall, and this garden is currently always in tomato.

Gerk pulls a large tomato plant through. On a perception of 10, something on the far side growls, snaps, and tugs the plant. Red and green tomatoes scatter. Gerk cuts the stalk with a dagger while Sylan tells him to keep a hand on the door. The rest of the plant snaps back, and whatever had it scrabbles, growls, and rams the closed door.

While Gerk's hand is on the shut door, it behaves like an ordinary door: he feels the impacts, and a hard enough hit would push him and swing it open. The door stays at the position his hand leaves it in. Shut, the far side is no longer the usual view through to the other space. He lets go during a lull. The outline dissipates, the growling stops, and the space returns to normal. He will not reopen it and risk letting the thing through.

Sylan reads that as confirmation that Gerk can keep working a door while he is operating it, including after he has closed it. He guesses the growling thing is the householder's pet and calls keeping it out the work of door guardians, a name they have not settled. Gerk hands out tomatoes as snacks. They decline a portal back to the stronghold and ride their mounts, arriving around midday. The morning's lesson is that Gerk can open these portals seemingly at will, with caveats.

plotSections.title: The illusion table
bullets: Walker has been meditating the whole time and still does not understand what he was told or what he is looking for. The aim is the puzzle Grixto put forward. Elrus asks for the eagle in Walker's pocket, tells him the repeated action now makes sense, and says the eagle has nothing to do with a mountain or a waterfall. He sets the hunched eagle with cavalry and infantry tokens on the square table, and asks for the cavalry markers, not the rams. Walker had guessed the eagle was a tuning fork.

Placing the hunched eagle makes the table flash. Four cardinal tokens become landmark representations, troop markings appear as a small semi-animated magical illusion, and a partial battlefield map fills in around them. Walker remembers Vecna tapping this same kind of piece on and off during their conversation, and Grixto taking a different hunched eagle from a table and leaving with the plan sorted.

The table is an illusion item that can project or reenact a battle or scenario if the right tokens are placed. The flat tokens they have are already at their usable limit; more known landmarks or other pieces would extend the map. How the tokens are made is unknown. Elrus reads this as how Grixto worked as a military planner, and says they are in over their heads. Walker thinks Grixto may have had a similar table in a command center where they first met him. He cannot settle the place name, and it is not confirmed.

plotSections.title: The offset obelisk and primal stones
bullets: On the map the obelisk sits fifteen degrees off where it should, which Elrus takes to mean a conveyance is there. Both he and Walker think it is worth checking.

Near a conveyance, Walker's wards and shields would be amplified, then return to normal a short time after he leaves. Channeling to force a stronger lasting effect is possible but untrained and could erase him. Elrus says that with more he could probably channel, and that they should meditate further.
Walker's gems already glow with energy he has been putting into them at the cost of exhaustion. Elrus once carried similar gems and gave them to other prospective riders.

Elrus offers primal stones: raw magic condensed into a stone. The maker would no longer be the only one directing it. A craftsperson could shape it into an item or call the energy, or it could be broken in desperation for a torrent of power. Condensing it could cost Walker part of himself. Walker wants to learn more. Elrus says he must pick a primal magic and asks whether he is attuned to any of the sources.

log: The DM sets the split-party clock: the faster group controls the timeline, Walker is on the Reach under a slower arrangement relative to the lighthouse group, and Walker's leftover scenes will be montaged when the party's one-week return window ends unless he ends early.
Five days and a morning have passed for the party since they left Walker on The Reach; Walker has lived eleven days, counted as just over two days of their time.

The DM notes Walker spoke with Vecna and may have joined a book club. His last beat was finding an earth, wind, sea, and fire sigil, and he has been deciphering a page of radially shifted landmarks—an obelisk, an island, a waterfall, and a mountain—as seen from the dragon rider guild's old tower.
Play resumes the same day in Carlkin's lighthouse with Ord, Gerk, and Sylan. Gerk keeps repairing the hole in the floor despite being told to stop, and is upset that Carlkin ignored his ask for help.
Sylan asks Carlkin if he has questions. Carlkin asks why they came. Sylan says they hoped Carlkin's long knowledge and presence would cover what they are facing, including the lich.

Carlkin, a former gatekeeper rather than a doorman, explains that former gatekeepers hid keystones and were not doormen, warns that redistributing keystones is strange, and urges them to deal immediately with the lich speaking to them telepathically.

He explains that Gerk can open and close his door from either side without a keystone, while keystone gates are situational, one-way, and bind the keystone into the gate. He distinguishes that portal from plane shift, dimension door, teleport, teleportation circles, and a Navi rod that teleports directionally across Atlas.

He tells Gerk to practice doors only in the woods or a large field, never underwater and not here, and to always shut a door he opens or it remains a gateway until space-time collapses. He recalls that they already nearly brought an abyssal leviathan into his shop, says he will mend the floor later, and drinks.

Sylan plans practice at the castle; Carlkin prefers the mountains, where the party mentions dragons and giants and Carlkin has heard the dragon is dead. Carlkin says the castle is farther than five hundred feet away.

They agree to leave and to make an appointment next time. Gerk admits he opened the doors to enter before he knew he should not, and refuses to risk opening more. Carlkin tells him to stay away from real doors and to put down the door that is dropping his arm.

Gerk tries to exit by the window because he took the warning not to use doors literally. He is told the ban was on his doorway ability rather than physical doors, and he rages when his mother's keepsake on his arm is dismissed. He breaks down over losing the last memory of his mother. Carlkin says Gerk's mother will not come to the portal, though everyone else will.
Gerk has to be dragged from the room. Sylan moves him back down through the floor with only the door and suggests he may need healing.
Sylan asks for a later appointment to examine a helm when a comrade returns. Carlkin agrees, via a runner. Sylan thanks him, closes the doors, and the group is outside at midday.

Walker, at the ruined Dragon Rider guild keep, compares a rotated landmark image and his notes with the cave drawings below. He refuses to return while Vecna is down there or to contact him through the book, and waits a couple of hours. Plymouth remains doing scribe work and etchings.
A notification pings that a deity has left the realm. Walker and Glimmen go back down.

The cave room is empty, the smell only faint, the chair pushed back, and Vecna's tapped troop marker is still on the table. The DM confirms a troop marker removed in the earlier vision would not still be in the room, and that the clockwise tilt of the cave sketches is a real tell.

The wall etchings run in sequence around the cave and do not line up with the cardinal directions. Walker treats that offset as a clue, and it is confirmed he is onto something. There is no carved map, no floor compass, and no manifesto. The table is a flat stone slab about four feet square. The room holds an empty roost, scattered troop markers, etchings of a place above, the table, and three extra stone chairs.

The markers depict cavalry knights, dragons, ranked pawns, and two sets of poker-chip tokens. Vecna's piece, which Walker is still holding, is a high-ranking hunched eagle with a decorative base. The marker removed in the earlier vision is absent. The group distinguishes the markers from Al Kurin and from the Raskina, identified in the vision as the sister-skin book.

Elrus, shadowing Walker, names the etchings: the grassy atoll, Mount Elcastar, and Monkey Falls with an old obsidian ley-line marker. He explains the Weave and ley lines as a crisscrossing magical boundary, finds that Walker knows neither, and says that gap has to close if Walker is going to beat Grixto.

Elrus reads the four shifted carvings as Grixto locating a ley line that moved, a convergence where a spell must be cast within feet of the point. A convergence bolsters spells and cheapens teleportation without being a road between planes. He links the site to Al Kurin and the Raskina for lichdom, notes that Viablis is an old landmark only rumored to be a ley line, and cannot explain the figurines without a map.

Walker asks how lichdom works. Elrus calls it an ancient ritual, usually using gems, and ties the Al Kurin, the convergence, and the Raskina together as the dangerous combination. They agree the convergence is worth visiting if their other business stalls. Elrus attributes hours feeling like weeks to time dilation, calls the eagle a legion standard tied to hobgoblin Grixto, has Walker pocket it, and tells him to meditate in the cave.
Elrus sets Walker to unwind the rituals Grixto put forward. Walker pockets the eagle and matches Elrus: seated, breathing through the nose and diaphragm, thinking about where he must go.

The scene cuts to the rest of the party outside Carlkin's lighthouse at midday on day six, with a day and a half remaining. Sylan proposes rest and, tomorrow, short-range practice of Gerk's doorway. Gerk floats a short jump to Carlkin's living room despite the ban on doors in the house; Sylan delays that until tomorrow.

Ord, Sylan, and Gerk go to the pub and find Ciri already drunk in the corner, stealth blown, surrounded by mugs. The tavern night passes with staff including a woman the DM calls Flavian, a finished cold-storage basement, locals, traders, and a wandering half-elf lutenist. The party sleeps it off.

They wake at Langdale Stronghold to shaking stone and fresh buns. Sylan and Walker clarify the check-in: one Midgar week of party time, with seven of Walker's days equaling one party day, so roughly forty-two Walker-days so far does not mean he is late.
After breakfast in the great hall, Sylan takes Gerk's training. Gerk accepts and asks if Ord will join. Ord and Ciri join. Ciri, who stayed in a tavern room, meets them on the stronghold path.

They rule out the stronghold living room and confirm there is no island in the lake. They consider the southern stream clearing from the hobgoblin search, skip the bees and old ruins, and settle on riding into the forest out of sight of the stronghold. Sylan tells the guards to inform Walker, expected to arrive on Glimmen, that the group went south into the forest and can be contacted, and asks Mahali to prepare food for the dragon.

Mid-morning they reach the forest outskirts. Asked about previously found runes marked by the red flag, they instead stop out of view to practice. They recall the doorway rules, and Gerk targets a point about twenty feet from the tavern door while Sylan grants Guidance.

On a 16, the door opens roughly a quarter mile southwest of that spot, with the tavern and most of the stronghold visible in the distance. Sylan steps through onto the tavern-to-New Navel road, startling three human traders with a mule cart about a football field away. The portal carries sound and a view of the forest side, but is otherwise an invisible, featureless door shape.

Gerk closes the door and targets Sylan about ten feet behind him. On a natural 20 the door opens exactly there, noticeable only by forest birdsong. They note that a person can be targeted, that knowing the general location helped, and that fondness might matter. Guards startle, then walk on, glancing back. Sylan hops back through and asks whether Gerk uses thought, memory, or fondness.

Ciri hides in the forest (stealth 7 against a 23) and later throws her voice before staying in a tree to watch. Gerk, eyes covered and guided by Sylan, tries to open close to her without knowing the exact spot and rolls a total of 4.

The door opens onto an explosion-filled trench where an orc and a human in mixed medieval and Renaissance dress level metal tubes and reach for a clay pot. Gerk shuts the door. A sulfur smell and a black smudge remain on the grass. He did not find Ciri. Sylan suggests a known location may be required, not only a person.

Sylan starts training on emotion or rage versus detailed memory of places. Gerk rejects being made angry. They recall that the door to Sylan worked because Gerk had just seen him. Sylan withholds a door home until the mission is done, names Halo Heart as a picture to hold, and walks Gerk through the frozen gatehouse at Volga, which they climbed: cold, tall, and mildly spooky. Gerk's memory of it is thin.

Gerk chooses Twin Peaks, a place he knows well with fond memories of friends, and aims for the upstairs hallway of Bouncing Betty outside the inn rooms, avoiding the street-facing front door. They argue the tavern's name and layout and whether another tavern was the one with the stage. They agree to try a short stop after the current training; they had said they would be in the forest, and Sylan notes Nawaka can message them.

With Sylan's Guidance, Gerk rolls 19 aiming from a Bouncing Betty bedroom to the upstairs hallway. Confusion pulls the doorway about twenty feet off onto the second-story loft of the rebuilt barn, above the stables and a central wagon, toward the more familiar memory of sleeping there and of a bard, a drunk wizard, and a levitated dead donkey or mule show that earned the party some gold. The group places their last visit long before the boat trip to Nyx, around collecting Plymouth and only then revealing the last keystone. Gerk closes the door; it clicks and vanishes.

Sylan praises the distance and accuracy for a liked place, then weighs more practice against unlocking something in Gerk. He contrasts Carlkin's claim that they could not open doors with Plymouth Gawater's claim that practice and time would let them use the keystones. Gerk rejects having a key put near him, citing a trick he will not fall for again. Sylan coaches him to use his hammer-swinging strength and open the door as hard as he can.

Sylan places a lantern about twenty feet away as a focus. Gerk faces away, pictures the lantern, rages, and opens the door with guidance, rolling a 17. An eighteen-foot-tall, seven-foot-wide door tears open onto the same forest about a quarter mile south. Birds disturb the far end, branches intersecting the doorway turn semi-translucent, and Gerk feels both this door and the far door.

Sylan and a hidden Ciri walk south through the woods instead of stepping through. They find the far door reaching into the canopy, with translucent cut branches and no crater or other destruction, then return through the portal. Sylan suggests fond memory may be required for accurate placement. Gerk is unsure of his range.

Gerk attempts a normal line-of-sight doorway about twenty-five feet away, past the lantern, with guidance, and rolls a 9. The door opens short, over the lantern. Because the earlier eighteen-foot doorway is still open, wind and a vacuum pull the lantern from one door into the other. Gerk closes both; the wind stops and branches crash to the south.

Sylan finds the intersecting limbs cleanly cut and unburned, recovers the dinged lantern, and warns that closing a door can slice whatever it intersects. They agree the shear is a hazard in crowds and when opening onto people, and stop further tests for now.
They decide not to doorway to Sylan's sister. They talk through Dana boosting the attempt and the fact that forcing the door makes it bigger. Gerk still does not know what ability he is using.

With Sylan's guidance, Gerk gently opens a doggy door toward the field in front of a tomato-grower's house and rolls an 18. The door is a few inches across and opens in the tomato plants. He hauls a tomato plant through; something on the other side growls and fights him for it. He cuts the stalk, it snaps back, and the creature scrabbles against the far side. He slams the door shut but keeps his hand on the handle.

While he touches it, the closed door stays and takes a ram like an ordinary door. It holds at the angle where his hand leaves it, and a hard shove while he is still holding it would swing it open. He lets go in a lull. The outline vanishes, the creature's noise stops, and he refuses to reopen it.
They snack on tomatoes, skip portaling home, and ride back to the stronghold, arriving around midday after a morning of portal practice.

The scene shifts to Walker, still meditating with Elrus on Grixto's puzzle. The eagle marker is set on the table, disconnected from the mountain and the waterfall, and Walker is asked for the cavalry markers.

Elrus takes the hunched-eagle marker and the cavalry and infantry tokens and lays them on a square table. Placing the hunched eagle flashes the table into a partial illusion map of four cardinal landmark tokens and smaller troop markers. Memory shows Vecna toggling such a piece, and Grixto taking a different hunched eagle from a table once the plan was set.

The projected obelisk is fifteen degrees off true, which Elrus reads as a conveyance at that spot. Wards would be stronger only while near the conveyance. Elrus warns Walker off untrained channeling and describes primal stones as stored raw magic he could try to condense, at the risk of losing part of himself. Elrus asks which primal source Walker is attuned to, and the scene ends before Walker answers.
